title: Rotate Image
descriptionHtml:
You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise).

You have to rotate the image in-place, which means you have to modify the input 2D matrix directly. DO NOT allocate another 2D matrix and do the rotation.

 

Example 1:

Input: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
Output: [[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]]

Example 2:

Input: matrix = [[5,1,9,11],[2,4,8,10],[13,3,6,7],[15,14,12,16]]
Output: [[15,13,2,5],[14,3,4,1],[12,6,8,9],[16,7,10,11]]

 

Constraints:

  • n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 20
  • -1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000
explanationMarkdown:
> **Thinking**
>
> The first idea is a new matrix with $\textit{matrix}[j][n-1-i] \gets \textit{matrix}[i][j]$. Correct, $O(n^2)$ time and space. $n \le 20$ fits, but the problem requires in-place.
>
> The extra matrix is the bottleneck. A $90^\circ$ clockwise turn factors into two in-place flips: reverse upside-down, then transpose across the main diagonal.
>
> $(i, j)$ goes to $(n-1-i, j)$, then to $(j, n-1-i)$ — the target. Two rounds of swaps, $O(1)$ extra space.

According to the problem requirements, we need to rotate $\textit{matrix}[i][j]$ to $\textit{matrix}[j][n - i - 1]$.

We can first flip the matrix upside down, i.e., swap $\textit{matrix}[i][j]$ with $\textit{matrix}[n - i - 1][j]$, and then flip the matrix along the main diagonal, i.e., swap $\textit{matrix}[i][j]$ with $\textit{matrix}[j][i]$. This way, we can rotate $\textit{matrix}[i][j]$ to $\textit{matrix}[j][n - i - 1]$.

The time complexity is $O(n^2)$, and the space complexity is $O(1)$, where $n$ is the side length of the matrix.
